module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 814

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/814](https://www.erdosproblems.com/814)
- [EFRS90] Erdős, P. and Faudree, R. J. and Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H., _Subgraphs of
  minimal degree k_. Discrete Math. (1990), 53--58.
- [Er91] Erdős, P., _Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory_. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, _Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory_.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [MNS17] Mousset, Frank and Noever, Andreas and Škorić, Nemanja, _Smaller subgraphs of minimum
  degree k_. Electron. J. Combin. (2017), Paper No. 4.9, 8.
- [Sa19] Sauermann, Lisa, _A proof of a conjecture of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp on
  subgraphs of minimum degree k_. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2019), 36--75.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos814

open scoped Classical in
/--
Let $k\geq 2$ and $G$ be a graph with $n\geq k-1$ vertices and
$$(k-1)(n-k+2)+\binom{k-2}{2}+1$$
edges. Does there exist some $c_k>0$ such that $G$ must contain an induced subgraph on at most
$(1-c_k)n$ vertices with minimum degree at least $k$?

The case $k=3$ was a problem of Erdős and Hajnal [Er91]. The question for general $k$ was a
conjecture of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp [EFRS90], who proved that such a subgraph
exists with at most $n-c_k\sqrt{n}$ vertices. Mousset, Noever, and Skorić [MNS17] improved
this to $n-c_k\frac{n}{\log n}$. The full conjecture was proved by Sauermann [Sa19], who proved
this with $c_k \gg 1/k^3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos814.lean#L81"]
theorem erdos_814 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ c > 0, ∀ n ≥ k - 1, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      G.edgeFinset.card = (k - 1) * (n + 2 - k) + (k - 2).choose 2 + 1 →
        ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.Nonempty ∧ (S.card : ℝ) ≤ (1 - c) * n ∧
          k ≤ (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).minDegree := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/-- The conclusion holds as soon as $G$ has at least $(k-1)(n-k+2)+ inom{k-2}{2}+1$ edges
(Sauermann [Sa19]). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos814.lean#L59"]
theorem erdos_814.variants.at_least :
    ∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ c > 0, ∀ n ≥ k - 1, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (k - 1) * (n + 2 - k) + (k - 2).choose 2 + 1 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
        ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.Nonempty ∧ (S.card : ℝ) ≤ (1 - c) * n ∧
          k ≤ (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).minDegree := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/-- Sauermann [Sa19] proved this with $c_k \gg 1/k^3$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_814.variants.sauermann :
    ∃ C > 0, ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ n ≥ k - 1, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (k - 1) * (n + 2 - k) + (k - 2).choose 2 + 1 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
        ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.Nonempty ∧ (S.card : ℝ) ≤ (1 - C / k ^ 3) * n ∧
          k ≤ (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).minDegree := by
  sorry

end Erdos814

findings.description: Line 67 of the docstring contains a literal backspace control character (byte 0x08). The `\b` of `\binom` was apparently read as an escape sequence, so the source text is `$(k-1)(n-k+2)+<BS>inom{k-2}{2}+1$` and renders as `+inom{k-2}{2}+1`. The docstring's edge-count formula therefore no longer shows the binomial coefficient $\binom{k-2}{2}$ that the Lean term `(k - 2).choose 2` encodes. The Lean statement itself is unaffected. `od -c` on the file shows `+ \b i n o m { k - 2 } { 2 } + 1`.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/814 (LaTeX source at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/814): "...a graph with $n\geq k-1$ vertices and \[(k-1)(n-k+2)+\binom{k-2}{2}+1\] edges". The main theorem's docstring in the same file (line 47) has the correct `\binom{k-2}{2}`.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the backspace byte plus `inom` on line 67 with `\binom`: `/-- The conclusion holds as soon as $G$ has at least $(k-1)(n-k+2)+\binom{k-2}{2}+1$ edges (Sauermann [Sa19]). -/`

reformulations.difference: The edge count $(k-1)(n-k+2)+\binom{k-2}{2}+1$ is written with truncated natural-number subtraction as `(k - 1) * (n + 2 - k) + (k - 2).choose 2 + 1`. The conclusion also carries an extra `S.Nonempty` conjunct.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the hypotheses k ≥ 2 and n ≥ k - 1 none of the subtractions truncate: n + 2 - k ≥ 1, k - 1 ≥ 1, k - 2 ≥ 0. So the ℕ value equals the integer formula; this is proved in Lean as a cast identity. It was also checked numerically against both $(k-1)(n-k+2)+\binom{k-2}{2}+1$ and Sauermann's $(k-1)n-t$ with $t=(k-2)(k+1)/2-1$ for 2 ≤ k ≤ 30 and k-1 ≤ n ≤ 60. `S.Nonempty` is redundant: Mathlib's `minDegree` of a graph on an empty vertex type is 0, so `k ≤ minDegree` with k ≥ 1 already forces S to be nonempty (proved in Lean). This also matches Sauermann's convention that 'minimum degree at least k' implies non-empty. Brute force further confirms that the `+1` sits exactly at the sharp threshold. With t_k(n) edges some graphs have only the whole graph as a core (e.g. the 12 labelled 5-cycles for k=2, n=5). With t_k(n)+1 edges every graph on n ≤ 6 vertices has a proper core.

reformulations.difference: It assumes at least the threshold number of edges (`≤ G.edgeFinset.card`), whereas the source problem and the main theorem say the graph has exactly that many edges.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Having exactly the threshold number of edges is a special case of having at least that many. Conversely, if G has at least m edges, delete edges to get G' ≤ G with exactly m edges on the same vertex set. The exact version gives S with G'[S] of minimum degree ≥ k. Since G'[S] ≤ G[S], `minDegree` can only go up. I proved `exact_iff_atLeast` in Lean with no sorry (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). It states that the right-hand side of `erdos_814` is equivalent to the statement of `erdos_814.variants.at_least`.

review.notes:
I checked all three declarations against erdosproblems.com/814 and the primary literature. The statements are faithful.

1. `erdos_814`
- It matches the erdosproblems text and Sauermann's Conjecture 1.2 exactly: for every k ≥ 2 there is c_k > 0 such that every graph on n ≥ k-1 vertices with (k-1)(n-k+2)+C(k-2,2)+1 edges has a vertex set S with |S| ≤ (1-c_k)n whose induced subgraph has minimum degree ≥ k.
- Quantifier order is ∀k ∃c ∀n ∀G. Elaborated types are k, n : ℕ and c : ℝ.
- The hypothesis cannot be met for n ∈ {k-1, k, k+1} and can be met from n = k+2 onward, exactly as the MNS17 footnote describes.
- `∃ c > 0` does not make the claim trivial: c ≥ 1 makes the conclusion impossible.
- `answer(True)` matches the source's 'PROVED, solved in the affirmative'. The `research solved` tag matches.

2. `erdos_814.variants.sauermann`
- It states c_k ≥ C/k^3 with an absolute C, uniformly in n. That is the correct reading of 'c_k ≫ 1/k^3'.
- Sauermann's Theorem 1.3 gives eps_k > 1/(10^4 k^3) for all n ≥ k-1, but only for k ≥ 3: its range of t is empty when k = 2.
- The k = 2 case is still true by an elementary argument: n+1 edges force a cycle of length ≤ 2(n+1)/3, and a brute force over n ≤ 6 agrees. The linked plby Lean proof also says it covers k = 2, t = -1. So the variant, and the `∀ k ≥ 2` in the main theorem, are true.

3. `formal_proof` records
- The links at L81 (`erdos_814`) and L59 (`erdos_814_atLeast`) point to statements identical to this file's. The differences are the `True ↔` wrapper, and a bound `[DecidableRel G.Adj]` instead of classical instances, which does not change the claim because such instances are unique.
- The supporting modules (~10.5k lines) contain no sorry, admit, axiom or native_decide. I did not build that project.
- A possible metadata improvement: the witness in the linked proof is c = 1/(10000 k^3). The underlying lemma would therefore also give `variants.sauermann` with C = 10^-4, but the exposed statement `Erdos814AtLeastStatement` only says ∃ c.

4. Status
- The teorth database lists formal_status 'unformalized' for 814. That field just means no formal proof is recorded there. It does not contradict the file, so I report no status issue.

The only defect found is the cosmetic backspace byte in the `at_least` docstring.
